title: Plants Per Field Calculator: Stand Counts
description: Calculate how many plants a field holds from row and in-row spacing with the Plants Per Field Calculator — plant population per acre and per field. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, corn on 30-inch rows at 6.9-inch in-row spacing plants 30,303 seeds per acre — so a 10-acre field is a 303,030-plant order before germination takes its cut.
quick_answer: The Plants Per Field Calculator turns row spacing and in-row spacing into plant population — plants per acre and for the whole field. Enter the two spacings and the field size and read the population: the number seed orders, transplant trays and yield models are all built from.

30-in rows × 6.9-in in-row: each plant owns 2.5 ft × 0.575 ft = 1.4375 sq ft; 43,560 ÷ 1.4375 = 30,303 plants per acre — squarely in the modern corn-belt range, which is why this pairing is the textbook one.
30 × 12 in spacing gives 17,424 per acre; 12 × 12 in (lettuce-style) gives 43,560 — the plant-per-acre number equals the square feet per acre when each plant owns exactly one square foot.

faq: Does the calculator handle rectangular plantings only?

The spacing model is a rectangular grid — the standard for row crops. Offset (triangular) planting packs about 15% more plants into the same spacings; orchards on triangular layouts should scale accordingly.
Plants per acre versus seeds per acre?
Population is the target stand. Seed rate adds germination and field losses on top — order more seeds than the population you want, by your seed lot's tested germination.
Turning headlands and tracks are unplanted. Subtract their share (often 3–8%) or enter the net planted acres — the calculator assumes every entered acre is planted.

Average the pattern into an effective row spacing (a twin-row pair on 30-in centres behaves like its centre spacing with two rows' in-row counts) — or compute per-band and scale. The simple grid covers most commercial patterns.
Centimetres and metres convert inside; European maize at 75 cm × 17 cm lands near 78,000 plants per hectare — the same geometry in the other dialect.
Identical math at larger scale: 20 × 20 ft trees are 109 per acre. The per-plant rectangle does not care whether the plant is corn or walnut.
How do I verify in the field?
Count plants in 1/1000th of an acre (17.4 ft of 30-in row) at several spots and average ×1,000 — the field audit this page's paper number invites.
